sentiment: The rocket falls on purpose, and someone waits below with open hands. Most of the work happens before the vessel exists.

stories.title: SpaceX catches the Starship to end Flight 15
stories.summary: A booster the size of a building falls back out of the sky and is caught by the thing that launched it. The spectacular part is the catch; the actual engineering was a decade of deciding exactly where it would come down, and building a hand to be there.

stories.title: How did Woz write the Apple 1 BASIC before building the computer?
stories.summary: He wrote the interpreter for a machine that did not exist yet, on paper and in his head, and it worked the first time it ran. That is the order most real work happens in — the vessel is the last part of the plan, not the first.

stories.title: Semicircle Packing
stories.summary: Set half-discs down one at a time and they arrange themselves into a pattern nobody drew in advance. Each piece only knows its own radius and what it bumped into — which turns out to be enough to cover the floor.
